$comment: The number each host event travels under on the service stream's return half (wire-v1.md, *The service stream*: EVENT).
WHAT AN EVENT IS. The host tells content something no request asked for -- a touch, a key, the soft
keyboard's text, a gamepad sample -- by calling a function on the engine's host bridge
(`globalThis[Symbol.for('Migo.hostBridge')]`). In the embedded runtime the host calls it in process
(engine/crates/runtime-v8/src/js_bindings.rs resolves each by the name below); in the external session
the host sends an EVENT record naming it by number, with the call's arguments as tagged values in the
function's parameter order, and the producer calls the same function of the same engine JavaScript. A
bytes value is passed as its ArrayBuffer, which is what the embedded bindings pass. Which calls a
HostCommand makes is decided once for both executions by engine/crates/core/src/runtime/input_route.rs.
HOW IT IS CHECKED. The host's table (engine/crates/core/src/runtime/host_events.rs) by a unit test that
reads this file; the producer's (platforms/apple/WebContent/PerformancePlus/src/host-events.mjs) by the
generator that stages the engine; and every name here must be a hook the embedded bindings resolve, by a
RULES. Append only: a number is never reused or renumbered.
